newsitem.title: USA: Study finds magnesium prevents problems in babies.
newsitem.headline: Study finds magnesium prevents problems in babies.

text.p: Severely underweight babies run a substantially lower risk of developing cerebral palsy and perhaps even mental retardation if their mothers get doses of magnesiun sulfate during pregnancy, a study said on Tuesday.

The finding was based on 1,097 very low birthweight babies born in Georgia between 1986 and 1988, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said. Such babies are almost always born prematurely and face a variety of developmental problems.
Among a portion of the babies whose mothers had been given the metallic element, only one had cerebral palsy and two were mentally retarded, the CDC report said.

That was "about a 90 percent lower prevalence of cerebral palsy and a 70 percent lower prevalance of mental retardation in magnesium sulfate-exposed children in comparison with unexposed children," it said.

Magnesium sulfate is sometimes given to pregnant women to prevent convulsions in those who develop high blood pressure or in an attempt to halt premature labor. Magnesium is found naturally in leafy green vegetables, nuts, whole grains, milk and seafood.
The study was published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.
